data.name: Raimunda
data.gender_notes: Raimunda is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: From the Latin word raemus, meaning recommendation or counsel. In Christianity, Raimunda is the name of several saints, including Raimunda of Merona and Raimunda of Toledo. The name Raimunda carries the meaning “Recommender, Counselor” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Raimunda usually hope their child will grow to embody recommender, counselor and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbol of guidance and wise counsel.
data.etymology: Raimunda belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Recommender, Counselor.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Raimunda total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

in_hebrew.name: ריימונדה
in_hebrew.meaning: שם מאזכר את ריימונד, אדם חזק ונאמן, ו-ה, כינוי יהוה
in_hebrew.long_meaning: שם המייצג אדם חזק, נאמן ואמין, תואר של ריימונד, הנביא, שהיה מלך של נאבל. השם נמצא בטקסטים ערבים וספרדיים. בספרות יהודית, השם נכתב כך: נבר עלוווהא, ריל עריייוא, אועוווא. באיבאבשבונ ריל אועוווא הלעיוה והעוווא.

in_greek.name: Ραιμούνδα
in_greek.meaning: ονομα που αναφέρεται στον Ραϊμόνδο, τον ισχυρό και τον πιστό, και η, ονομα των Θεού
in_greek.long_meaning: ονομα που αναφέρεται σε άνδρα ισχυρό, πιστό και αμετακίνητο, όπως ο Ραϊμόνδος, ο ναβαλιανός βασιλιάς. το ονομα εμφανίζεται σε αραβικά και ισπανικά κείμενα. στην εβραϊκή βιβλιογραφία, το ονομα γράφεται ως: נבר עלוווהא, ריל עריייוא, אועוווא. באיבאבשבונ ריל אועוווא הלעיוה והעוווא.

in_latin.name: Raimunda
in_latin.meaning: nomen quod referuntur ad Raimundum, virum fortem et fidem, et ha, nomen Dei
in_latin.long_meaning: nomen quod significat virum fortissimum et fidem, sicut Raimundus, rex Nabalis. nomen inventum est in textibus Arabicis et Hispanicis. in litteratura Hebraica, nomen scribitur ut: ריימונד, ראימונד, ראימונד. Raimundus, rex Nabalis, fuit vir fortis et fidelis. haec nomen usitata sunt in Ecclesia Christiana ab initio.

in_english.name: Raimunda
in_english.meaning: name that refers to Raimund, a strong and faithful man, and ha, name of God
in_english.long_meaning: name that means a very strong and faithful man, like Raimundus, the king of Nabalis. the name is found in Arabic and Spanish texts. in Hebrew literature, the name is written as: ריימונד, ראימונד, ראימונד. Raimundus, the king of Nabalis, was a very strong and faithful man. this name was used in the Christian Church from the beginning.

data.cultural_impact: The name Raimunda holds a rich cultural history in Christianity, where it has been borne by several saints. It is a reminder of the importance of seeking counsel and guidance in our lives. Through these saints, Raimunda represents the role of spiritual advisors and the wisdom they impart.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Raimunda is deeply spiritual, reminding us of the importance of seeking guidance from those who have lived a virtuous life. Each saint with this name serves as a beacon of hope and spiritual growth. The name carries the weight of their wisdom and the lessons they have to share. Ultimately, Raimunda is a symbol of the power of seeking spiritual advice and the impact it can have on our own spiritual journey.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Raimunda is a name derived from the Latin word "Raimundus," which means "protection from God" or "advised by God." It symbolizes the belief in divine guidance and God's protective care, reminding the bearer of their connection to the divine.

historical_references.reference: Raimunda of Carcassonne was a French saint who lived in the 13th century. She was the daughter of Count Raimond IV of Toulouse and Almodis of La Marche. According to legend, Raimunda was raised in a convent and later became an abbess herself. She was known for her piety and miraculous healings.

Raimunda of Sassovia was a German saint who lived in the 10th century. She was the daughter of Margrave Raimund I of the Nordgau and Gertrude of the Wetterau. According to legend, Raimunda was a virgin who was martyred during the Magyar invasion of Germany. She is venerated as a patron saint of childbirth and midwives.

It is frequently featured on social media platforms where parents share their naming journeys, and Christian name websites where expectant parents research meaningful Biblical names. The name bridges traditional Christian values with modern faith identity, making it relevant for contemporary families seeking names with deep spiritual and Biblical significance.
